n: After the destruction of 3:12, a glorious reversal: in the last days the Lord’s temple will be lifted high above all mountains, and people will stream to it. These verses (1–3) are nearly identical to Isaiah 2:2-4, quoted in 2 Nephi 12.

f.w: in the last days
the mountain of the house of the LORD
f.g: Latter-day Saints often apply this to temples, including the Salt Lake Temple in the tops of the mountains.

n: Nations will urge one another to go up to God’s house to learn His ways. God’s law and word will go out from Zion and Jerusalem — two centers of truth.

f.w: he will teach us of his ways
the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem
f.g: Latter-day Saints sometimes read this as two world capitals of the Lord’s kingdom in the Millennium.

n: The Lord will judge among nations and settle disputes. Weapons will be turned into farming tools, and war will end. This describes the peace of the Millennium.

f.w: they shall beat their swords into plowshares
pruninghooks

n: Micah adds a homey picture Isaiah doesn’t: each family resting under its own vine and fig tree, with nothing to fear. Peace means personal security and enough to live on.

f.w: every man under his vine and under his fig tree

n: Other nations may follow their gods for now, but we will walk in the name of the Lord forever. A personal commitment of loyalty.

f.w: we will walk in the name of the LORD our God

n: In that day the Lord will gather the lame, the outcasts, and those He had disciplined. God’s kingdom welcomes the wounded.

f.w: her that halteth
I will gather her that is driven out

n: The weak will become a remnant, and the scattered a strong nation. The Lord Himself will reign from Mount Zion forever.

f.w: the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion

n: Jerusalem, the watchtower of the flock, will receive back its former kingdom and dominion, as in David’s days.

f.w: tower of the flock
f.g: Hebrew Migdal-eder — a lookout tower for shepherds near Bethlehem (Genesis 35:21).

f.w: the first dominion
f.g: The former kingdom, as under David and Solomon.

n: Back to the present: Why are you crying out? Do you have no king or counselor? Jerusalem is in agony like a woman in labor.

f.w: a woman in travail
f.g: In labor, giving birth — pain that leads to new life.

n: Jerusalem must suffer exile — leave the city, live in the open field, and go to Babylon. But there the Lord will rescue her. Micah foresaw Babylon over a century in advance, while Assyria was the great power.

f.w: thou shalt go even to Babylon
there the LORD shall redeem thee

n: Many nations gather against Zion, eager to see it desecrated.

f.w: let our eye look upon Zion

n: But they don’t know the Lord’s plan: He is gathering them like sheaves onto a threshing floor to be judged. The Savior quoted verses 12–13 to the Nephites.

f.w: he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor

n: Zion is told to rise and thresh like an ox with iron horns and bronze hoofs. The spoils of the nations will be dedicated to the Lord of all the earth.

f.w: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion
I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD
